questions.title: Print Struct Point Members
questions.description:
Define a struct Point with members x and y. Read two integers x and y, store them in a struct Point variable, then print them space-separated.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers x and y.

Output Format:
The two integers space-separated.

Constraints:
-10^9 <= x, y <= 10^9

questions.title: Access Student Record Fields
questions.description:
Define a struct Student with members id and age. Read the id and age, then print them in the format "ID=<id> Age=<age>".

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers id and age.

Output Format:
The string "ID=<id> Age=<age>".

Constraints:
1 <= id <= 10^9, 1 <= age <= 150

questions.title: Nested Date in Event
questions.description:
Define a struct Date with members day, month, year. Define a struct Event that contains a Date as a nested member. Read the day, month, and year, then print them in day/month/year format.

Input Format:
A single line with three space-separated integers: day month year.

Output Format:
The string "<day>/<month>/<year>".

Constraints:
1 <= day <= 31, 1 <= month <= 12, 1900 <= year <= 2100

questions.title: Array of Student Records
questions.description:
Define a struct Student with members id and age. Read n, then n pairs of (id, age). Print each pair on its own line in the format "<id> <age>".

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Next n lines: each line has two space-separated integers (id and age).

Output Format:
n lines, each containing "<id> <age>".

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 1 <= id <= 10^9, 1 <= age <= 150

questions.title: Pointer to Struct Access
questions.description:
Define a struct Point with members x and y. Create a struct Point variable and a pointer to it. Read x and y into the struct via the pointer (using ->), then print the values via the pointer.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers x and y.

Output Format:
The two integers space-separated.

Constraints:
-10^9 <= x, y <= 10^9

questions.title: Union Data Storage
questions.description:
Define a union Data with an int member i and a float member f. Read an integer v, store it in the union's int member, then print the int member's value.

Input Format:
A single line containing one integer v.

Output Format:
The integer v.

Constraints:
-10^9 <= v <= 10^9

questions.title: Manhattan Distance from Origin
questions.description:
A navigation tool computes the Manhattan distance from the origin to a point. Define a struct Point with members x and y. Pass the struct by value to a helper function that returns |x| + |y|.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers x and y.

Output Format:
The Manhattan distance as a single integer.

Constraints:
-10^9 <= x, y <= 10^9

questions.title: Rectangle Area via Struct
questions.description:
A graphics utility computes the area of a rectangle. Define a struct Rectangle with members width and height. Read width and height, then compute and print width * height.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers width and height.

Output Format:
The area as a single integer.

Constraints:
1 <= width, height <= 10^4

questions.title: Inventory Total Quantity
questions.description:
A store inventory lists n items, each with an integer id and a quantity. Read n, then n (id, quantity) pairs. Compute the total quantity of all items.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Next n lines: each line has two space-separated integers (id and quantity).

Output Format:
The total quantity as a single integer.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 1 <= id <= 10^6, 1 <= quantity <= 10^4

questions.title: Person with Nested Address
questions.description:
A person record contains a nested Address struct (street_num and city_code). Read id, street_num, and city_code into a Person, then print in the format "ID=<id> Street=<street> City=<city>".

Input Format:
A single line with three space-separated integers: id street_num city_code.

Output Format:
The string "ID=<id> Street=<street> City=<city>".

Constraints:
1 <= id <= 10^6, 1 <= street_num <= 10^4, 1 <= city_code <= 999

questions.title: Bank Account Withdrawal Check
questions.description:
A bank account has an account number and an integer balance. Read the account number, the current balance, and a withdrawal amount. If the balance is sufficient, deduct the withdrawal and print the new balance; otherwise print "INSUFFICIENT".

Input Format:
A single line with three space-separated integers: account_no balance withdrawal.

Output Format:
The new balance, or "INSUFFICIENT".

Constraints:
1 <= account_no <= 10^9, 0 <= balance <= 10^9, 0 <= withdrawal <= 10^9

questions.title: Student Average Marks Calculator
questions.description:
A student record contains an id and marks in 3 subjects. Read id and three marks. Compute and print the integer average (total / 3 using integer division).

Input Format:
A single line with four space-separated integers: id m1 m2 m3.

Output Format:
The integer average of the three marks.

Constraints:
1 <= id <= 10^9, 0 <= m1, m2, m3 <= 100

questions.title: Top Scorer Finder Manual
questions.description:
A school has n students (id and 3 marks). Find the id of the student with the highest total marks. Ties are broken by the earliest position in input (smallest index). Manual traversal (no qsort).

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Next n lines: each line has four space-separated integers (id m1 m2 m3).

Output Format:
The id of the top-scoring student.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 1 <= id <= 10^9, 0 <= m1, m2, m3 <= 100

questions.title: Move Point via Struct Pointer
questions.description:
A graphics engine moves a Point by (dx, dy) using a helper that takes a struct Point pointer. Read x, y, dx, dy, then print the new coordinates.

Input Format:
A single line with four space-separated integers: x y dx dy.

Output Format:
The new x and y space-separated.

Constraints:
-10^9 <= x, y, dx, dy <= 10^9

questions.title: Tagged Union Value Storage
questions.description:
A tagged union stores either an int or a float selected by a tag. Read tag (0 for int, 1 for float). If tag is 0, read an int and print it; if tag is 1, read a float and print it with 2 decimal places.

Input Format:
Line 1: an integer tag (0 or 1).
Line 2: if tag is 0, an integer; if tag is 1, a floating-point number.

Output Format:
The value (integer for tag 0; float with 2 decimals for tag 1).

Constraints:
tag in {0, 1}; for tag 0, -10^9 <= v <= 10^9; for tag 1, -10^9 <= v <= 10^9

questions.title: Rectangle Area Function
questions.description:
A geometry library computes rectangle area via a function that takes a Rectangle struct by value. Read width and height, then print the area computed by the helper.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers width and height.

Output Format:
The area width * height.

Constraints:
1 <= width, height <= 10^4

questions.title: Student Age and Average Computation
questions.description:
A student record contains an id, a nested birth Date (day, month, year), and marks in 3 subjects. Compute the student's age as 2024 minus birth year, and the integer average of the three marks. Print "<age> <avg>".

Input Format:
A single line with seven space-separated integers: id day month year m1 m2 m3.

Output Format:
The age and the average, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= id <= 10^9, 1900 <= year <= 2024, 0 <= m1, m2, m3 <= 100

questions.title: Student Sort by Marks Manual
questions.description:
A teacher has n students (id and marks). Sort the students in ascending order of marks using a manual sort (no qsort). Print the sorted ids separated by single spaces. Ties preserve the original input order.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Next n lines: each line has two space-separated integers (id and marks).

Output Format:
The sorted ids, space-separated on a single line.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 1 <= id <= 10^9, 0 <= marks <= 100

questions.title: Sum of X via Struct Pointer Array
questions.description:
A geometry analyzer has n points (x, y). Build an array of struct Point pointers (each ptrs[i] points to pts[i]) and use the pointer array (with ->) to compute the sum of all x-coordinates.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Next n lines: each line has two space-separated integers (x and y).

Output Format:
The sum of all x-coordinates.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, -10^4 <= x, y <= 10^4

questions.title: Count Passed Students Function
questions.description:
An exam grader counts how many students passed (marks >= 40). Write a function that takes an array of Student structs and the count n, and returns the number of passed students. Read n, then n (id, marks) pairs, then print the count.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Next n lines: each line has two space-separated integers (id and marks).

Output Format:
The number of students who passed.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 1 <= id <= 10^9, 0 <= marks <= 100
